paper.title_en: Variational quantum circuit learning for bilinear control of nonlinear Schrödinger dynamics
paper.abstract_en: Variational quantum circuits have emerged as expressive learning architectures for hybrid quantum-classical optimization. In this work, we developed a dual-channel variational quantum framework for bilinear optimal control of the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation. A parameterized quantum circuit with time reuploading is used to generate two control fields, which modulate the displacement and confinement terms. We proved global well-posedness and existence of optimal controls in a weighted energy space, via an energy identity requiring no time differentiability of the controls. Also, we show that the realizable controls are trigonometric polynomials with frequencies drawn from a finite set. This frequency set grows linearly with the circuit depth. However, this family is not dense in the space of continuous functions because the readout imposes a uniform bound on the amplitude of the controls. Numerical experiments are demonstrated over twenty restarts, matched in parameter count, amplitude bounds, budget, and initial occupancy, to show that the quadratic channel raises the terminal fidelity from 0.833 to 0.999. Compared with equal-size Fourier, chopped-random-basis, and spline parameterizations, the circuit achieves comparable fidelity while using approximately half the control energy.
